figures.finding: The Screenwriters Association's 2019 fair-remuneration guidelines recommend minimum film script fees by budget: under Rs 5 crore, Rs 3 lakh for the story, 5 lakh for the screenplay and 4 lakh for the dialogue (12 lakh in all); Rs 5 to 15 crore, 6, 10 and 8 lakh (24 lakh); over Rs 15 crore, 9, 15 and 12 lakh (36 lakh); a recommendation, not an agreement producers' bodies have signed.

value.producerExample: Excel Entertainment: the writer may take a lower base fee plus 2% of profit

figures.applies: India, Hindi film screenwriters, from June 2019; television and streaming fees not set.

sources.said: It has recommended that if the production budget of a film is less than Rs. 5 crore, the story writer should be paid at least Rs. 3 lakh, screenplay writer at least Rs. 5 lakh, and dialogue writer at least Rs. 4 lakh.
For a film with a production budget of Rs. 5-15 crore, the story writer should be paid a minimum of Rs. 6 lakh, screenplay writer Rs. 10 lakh, and dialogue writer Rs. 8 lakh.

In such cases, the recommended minimum fees are Rs. 9 lakh for story, Rs 15 lakh for screenplay, and Rs. 12 lakh for dialogues. In other words, the total fee for the whole script would have to be at least Rs. 36 lakh.

For a film with below Rs 5 crore budget, the minimum fee for script is Rs 12 lakh (Rs 3 lakh for story, Rs 5 lakh for screenplay, Rs 4 lakh for dialogue), for film with Rs 5-15 crore budget, the minimum fee for script is Rs 24 lakh.

figures.finding: No agreement between writers and producers sets screenwriters' pay or terms in India: the minimum basic contract the SWA drafted for film, television and lyrics was negotiated with the Producers Guild, the IFTPC and broadcasters without result; in 2019 one producer (Ritesh Sidhwani of Excel Entertainment) signed on to the guidelines, and in 2023 the SWA was still seeking to negotiate a standard contract collectively.

negotiatedWith: Film and TV Producers Guild of India
Indian Film and TV Producers Council
value.status2023: SWA seeking collective negotiation with producers and platforms

figures.applies: India, film and television screenwriters, 2019 to 2023 (no later agreement found).

sources.said: Insist on the model Minimum Basic Contract proposed by the Screenwriters Association. … The producers’ bodies are yet to approve the model contract but it’s strongly recommended by SWA. … The aim of all four MBC sub-committees (Film, TV, Lyric & Web) is to draft the Minimum Basic Contracts (model contracts) and the minimum rate cards, and ensure, via collective bargain and negotiations, that they are accepted as standard industry practices.

A minimum basic contract was drafted some years ago for film, as well as television writers, and for lyricists. Negotiations had begun with the Film and TV Producers Guild, the Indian Film and TV Producers Council as well as some broadcasters.
But for different reasons, they couldn't reach a satisfactory conclusion.
Filmmaker Ritesh Sidhwani has turned out to be the first person from Bollywood to sign on for the guidelines by Screenwriters Association.
The union wants to negotiate with the producers collectively on behalf of their members.

According to the union, the basic contract will protect writers from arbitrary terminations, improper crediting and introduce a minimum fixed pay at least for films. The minimum fixed pay will be commensurate with the budget of the film, the union says.

Raj Shekhar, General Secretary of the Screenwriters Association … A writer starts their work first, but they get paid last; the delays are of 60 to 90 days. … Our efforts have been to resolve this, and the work on the Minimum Basic Contract is ongoing,

figures.finding: Indian screenwriters' royalties beyond the cinema hall are collected by the Screenwriters Rights Association of India, registered as a copyright society on 30 December 2024: about 600 to 680 members, lifetime membership Rs 5,000 plus GST for a writer (about Rs 6,600 all in); theatrical earnings attract no royalty, licensing to streaming or television does.

value.name: Screenwriters Rights Association of India (SRAI)
value.royaltyBase: non-theatrical uses (streaming licences, broadcast); box office excluded

figures.applies: India, authors of story, screenplay and dialogue, from 2025.

sources.said: SRAI’s registration as a copyright society on 30 December 2024 gave them, for the first time, a collective body that can negotiate tariffs, collect royalties, receive money from foreign copyright societies, and distribute it to writers and their legal heirs.
SRAI currently has around 680 members.
To become a member, a writer has to pay a one-time fee of about Rs 6,600, which includes GST, e-KYC, e-signing, and deed-related costs.

“Statutorily, the money made out of the box office doesn’t attract [royalty]. The moment [a film] gets licensed to Netflix or Amazon, then on that licensing fee, SRAI can charge a royalty,” Ranganath said.
SRAI currently has around 600 members — about 580 writers and 20 producer-owners.
Membership is lifetime ₹5,000 plus GST for writers and ₹10,000 plus GST for producer-owners.

figures.finding: The Screenwriters Association (Mumbai) charges a one-off INR 21,000 for life membership, INR 7,620 plus INR 120 a year for regular members, and INR 4,216 (associate) or INR 3,216 (fellow) for three years; regular and life membership need a released film, festival film, TV or streaming credit, associate a paid contract, a screenwriting course of a year or an additional-writer credit, and fellow only proof of identity.
figures.applies: Screenwriters Association (SWA), India, as published on its website read 2026-11-01; the Executive Committee may revise the fees.
